groups.title: Prisma's schema-first approach and type generation
groups.question: You are modeling a blog with users, posts and tags in Prisma, and a teammate asks where all the typed database methods come from. Explain how Prisma turns the schema into a client and how relations are modeled.

followUps.How Prisma generates a typed client from: Where do the typed methods on the Prisma client come from, and when must you regenerate them?
followUps.Prisma relations: one-to-many and many-t: How would you model posts that belong to one user, and posts that have many tags?

evidence.text: Prisma reads schema.prisma and generates a TypeScript client from it.
Every model, field and relation gets types, so queries are checked and autocompleted.
After changing the schema, the client must be regenerated for the types to match.

notEnough: Only saying Prisma is a typed ORM.

evidence.text: A one-to-many relation stores a foreign key on the many side, such as authorId on Post.
Both models get relation fields so you can navigate either way.
Many-to-many relations use a join table, which Prisma can manage implicitly or you can define explicitly when it needs extra fields.

groups.title: Prisma migrations and the development workflow
groups.question: You added a field to a model and your post list page now makes 51 database queries. Explain how you would change the schema safely and fix the slow query.

followUps.prisma migrate dev: generating, naming,: What does prisma migrate dev do, and why commit the migration files?
followUps.N+1 query problem and how to fix it with: What is the N+1 problem here and how does include fix it?

evidence.text: It compares the schema with the database and writes a SQL migration for the difference.
It applies the migration and regenerates the client.
Migration files are committed so every environment applies the same changes in order.

notEnough: Only saying it updates the database.

evidence.text: Loading a list and then querying each item's relation separately makes one query per item.
include loads the related data together with the list.
That turns many queries into one or two, which is much faster.

notEnough: Only saying N+1 means too many queries.

groups.title: Prisma CRUD operations in tRPC procedures
groups.question: Your tRPC procedures list posts with paging and create an order that must also reduce stock. Explain how you would write these Prisma queries correctly.

followUps.findMany with where, orderBy, take, and: How do take and skip paginate, and when is cursor pagination better?
followUps.Prisma transactions for multi-step atomi: Why must creating the order and reducing stock happen in a transaction?

evidence.text: findMany uses where to filter and orderBy to sort.
take limits the number of rows and skip jumps past earlier pages.
Cursor pagination continues from the last item and stays fast on large tables, where skipping many rows gets slow.
A transaction runs several writes so they all succeed or all fail.
If one step fails, earlier steps are rolled back, leaving no half-finished data.
Interactive transactions allow logic between steps, such as checking stock before writing.

notEnough: Only saying transactions keep data safe.

groups.title: Prisma Studio and seeding for development
groups.question: New developers on your team need realistic data locally and a way to look at the database without writing SQL. Explain the tools you would use and how to make seeding safe to run again.

followUps.Prisma Studio: browsing and editing data: What is Prisma Studio useful for during development?
followUps.Writing an idempotent seed script with u: Why use upsert in a seed script?

evidence.text: Prisma Studio opens a web interface to browse tables and records.
You can filter and edit rows without writing SQL.
It helps check what is actually in the database while developing.

notEnough: Only saying it is a database GUI.

evidence.text: A seed script should be safe to run many times.
upsert creates a record if it does not exist and leaves or updates it if it does.
That prevents duplicate records or unique constraint errors on the second run.

notEnough: Only saying seeding adds test data.
